[quote=tirakan;61019481][i][b]Encrypted Message to [nation]Nordiheim[/nation][/b][/i]

It was the same bunker, the TIS used just a few days ago to contact Alaqar. The room was silent in a way that makes your thoughts, alongside to the white noise from the computers unbearably loud. There are no windos, flags, maps, or anything you could associate with Tirakan. But in the end of the room, a beamer lit up the wall with a projected picture of trade date between Nordiheim and Tirakan. Right next to that was a long list of infrastructure notification, reactor maintenance schedules and procurement channels. The data did not belong to Tirakan. The TIS had pored over these lists for months, to make sure that what they've expected since the 1990s already, is really true. Because making a mistake now, will cost the nations credibility. And many jobs. And many lifes.

"They built it the same way we did," said someone finally. It didn't really come off like an accusation. More like a conclusion, with a little bit of admiration.

"We've been suspecting it since decades now, what did you expect?", a man murmurs, leaned back in his seat, his legs rested on the table infront of him.

Nordiheims civil nuclear energy projects had always been public. They were transparent enough to satisfy the inspectors, opaque enough to allow for leeway. It was within such leeways that the truth had been uncovered by the TIS, but not with waterproof plans or documents, but in timing, in redundancies, in overlaps of procurement that only added up to one purpose if it wasnt energy production. To the TIS, figuring it out, was a pretty easy game. After all Tirakans own nuclear journey, begun unknowingly contemporaneous to Nordiheims, under the same cover of a civil nuclear energy project. The same idea, the same schedules, the same date. It was a reflection of exactly that, what the Tiraki Intelligence Service has been made for in the first place.

Suddenly the doors swing up, and two men in black suits followed by a handful of security guards march into the room. In shock both men, just casually chatting a second ago, take their feet off the desk and straighten up. Immediately a channel is opened, and projected onto the wall onto the end of the room. It was an old encryption line agreed upon with Nordiheim, for emergencies years before the civil war kicked off. After all men inside the room watch the bar load to its fullest once, one man in suite, TIS general director Ahman Befir, stepped forward, and the personell immediately took seat behind dimly glowing PC screens. 

"All set?", he asked and cleared his throat after a nodding response from both men next to him ready to type down his words.

[b][ENCRYPTED TRANSMISSION TO NORDIHEIM - MIDGARD][/b]

To the highest council of Nordiheim,

This message is sent with the expectation of discretion. Its existence is not intended for acknowledgment beyond the recipients of this channel.

Tirakan has, over the course of decades, maintained close commercial and technical relations with Nordiheim. Through these relations, and through long-term observation rather than intrusion or distrust, we have come to understand that our two states share more than trade corridors.

Tirakan is aware that Nordiheim has, since the late 1980s, maintained a nuclear weapons program concealed beneath the framework of its civil nuclear energy sector. This awareness is not the result of a single incident, breach, or disclosure, but of experienced pattern recognition conducted over many years. We state this plainly so there is no misunderstanding.

Tirakan has walked the same path.

We contact you, to reveal that Tirakan too, is attempting to develop nuclear weapons, in the face of modern days threats. Our own nuclear weapons program began in 1988. It survived years of internal compartmentalization, and later, disruption caused by civil war. During that period, the Free Republic of Naerim, which was the faction reunifying the country and re-newing the Nordiheim-Tirakan trade pact, retained control of key facilities and accelerated development out of necessity rather than ambition. Today, Tirakan has regained political stability, and our program has entered its final developmental phase.

We are contacting Nordiheim now because circumstances have changed. In the face of international pressure, nations attempting to reveal the truth behind Tirakans nuclear weapons program, silence will not bring us far in certainty. It is inefficiency, that we've been willing to endure facing no time pressure. But this has ended now.

We believe both our states face the same reality. Pursuing nuclear deterrence alone increases risk and vulnerability. Cooperation, even if limited, reduces both.

Tirakan therefore proposes covert cooperation between our nuclear weapons programs, specifically in areas where parallel development has already occurred and mutual benefit is evident. This cooperation would be strictly secret, state-to-state, and restricted to a minimal circle of trusted scientific and strategic authorities. Nothing public.

If Nordiheim is willing to explore this cooperation, we request confirmation through this channel only. Further structure and safeguards can be discussed once intent is established.

If you choose not to respond, this message will not be repeated and never to be found again.

My name is Ahman Befir, general director of the Tiraki Intelligence service. 
I talk in the name of my country: We expect your response soon.

[b][TRANSMISSION ENDS][/b][/quote]

[b]Encrypted Message to[/b] [nation]Tirakan[/nation].

[spoiler=[u]A Responce from much Consideration.[/u]]
[b][u]Midgard - Council hall.[/u][/b]
The council satt around their round table were they read over and discused the message that the Shadow Keepers had delivered to them not to long ago with some having questions to ask, the first to ask it was the minister of Midland, Mr. Siggurd Haraldson.
[i]So would the good minister of war perhaps have a explanation as to how the good people over in Tirakan have managed to find out about a research project that was supposed to be secret to my understanding?[/i]

The minister of war, Grand general Thormod Thormodson III, looked over at Siggurd with a look of annoyance and a clear indication that he most likely knew exactly how it could have happened.
[i]Almoust two decades of military budget cuts and most likely the shady 90s.[/i]
He said as he leaned back and waited for their questions that he knew was comming.

The other ministers waited for a bit, fully expecting Thormod to ellaborate, but when it become obvious he wouldn't they started asking him more questions, starting with the minister of Ostland Lode Miason.
[i]What do you mean with that? And were is the rest of the explanation?[/i]
Jiemba Turidson, the minister of Sorland, would add his own question on top of Lodes.
[i]Budget cuts and someting about "shady 90s" is not a good enough explanation general![/i]
The minister of Law, Judge Tau Bjornason, would also voice his diseproval of the good generals short answer.
[i]As you can clearly see and hear General Thormod a better answer is needed and [b]must[/b] be given, how can you be so sure that it was in the 90s and not more recent?[/i]
Most of the other ministers would ask similar questions demanding a longer and more satisfying answer from the calm, though anoyed looking, Grand General.

One person that asked a more calm question was the old minister of Aboria, Chief Adoni Bardoson, his question was a simple one.
[i]I asume that your short answer is related to the rather embarrassing incident that ledd to the [u]"Millennium Crackdown"[/u]?[/i]

Grand General Thormod would camly look over at the old Chief, satisfied that atleast on of the other ministers seemed to have figured out what he was eluding to, as he began explaining it in more detail to the other ministers that seemed to not fully understand, or even know, what the [u]"Millennium Crackdown"[/u] was and meant.
[i]As some of you might remember, like the good Chief here, we had a massive crackdown on security in our nation when we entered the year of 2000, this was someting that was long overdue because of the lax security in our nation that was caused by budget defecits and shortcuts that had been done trough the 60s and 70s as we had to focus most of the available resources on not only saving our economy at the time but preventing it from suffering a potential collapse, but even though it had been saved by the end of the 80s the budget of our military and the intelligence branches did not see a increase wich led to the general security of our nation to be severly lacking in the 90s.

This was revealed in a rather painfull and embarrasing incident that happened 1998 were a small group of joung servicemen that was part of the Red Mountain complex decided to try and play a stupid joke on a officer that they did not like.[/i]
Thormod gave a signal to his minister team who started to give the other ministers a folder containing pappers on said incident for them to look at before he continued speaking.
[i]These young and foolish men would sneak into one of the vaults containing balistic warheads for our ICMs and "steal" one of these warheads with the help of some friends that they then hid in their barracks unit.
Their plan was for the officer that they diden't like, a older man that was nearing retirement age, to find out about it being gone and run to his supperiors to repport about it, they would then quickly place the warhead back in its spot before he could bring people back to confirm that the warhead was gone making him seem like a fool that was perhaps going a bit senile in his old age, no matter how stupid their little idea was is not how it ended up going.
The warhead was not discovered to be missing at all and what was supposed to be someting that would be over in less then perhaps a week turned to months, when about a year had gone by with no signs of their little "warhead disaperance" being noticed they decided as a group, brought on by what they claimed to be growing fealing of national duty, to go directly to the minister of war, old General Odin at the time, and tell him exactly what they had been able to essentialy pull off without anyone noticing, bringing the warhead with them mind you as proof.[/i]

[i]At the time I was part of the ministry team of the then minister of war, old General Odin "Staalneve" Jarlson, when those men came into his office and presented their case and let me tell you that it was a rather shocking event to look directly at a balistic warhead that someone had joust taken out of what should have been the most secure facility of any kind in our nation without anyone noticing.
I remember that old Odin kept rather calm under it all, and he was a man known to have quite the rage and foul language when someting went wrong when it shoulden't, and asked the young men to show him everyting and help him gatter the neceseary evidence, I learned later that he was keeping his calm to not scare those men off and get what he needed to litteraly [u]force[/u] the council at that time to finaly give him the funding and free reins to clean up the military from head to toe in the most dramatic way that our nation had ever seen, starting with the Shadow Keepers so that he could use them to ensure not a singel person was left in a position that they did not belong in.
From what I remember there was even some executions of people that was found guilty of treason towards our nation, so I would not be supriced at all if the nation of Tirakan managed to aquire information on our nuclear weapons program during the 90s.[/i]

Thormod motions his hand towards the papers that the other ministers are reading through.
[i]This is what led to the [u]"Millennial Crackdown"[/u] as we now know it as and that will be my answer to your questions of how it could have possibly happened, though I will of course have let the Shadow Keepers go through our security as a precausion but I doupt that they will find any indication of a breach in our security as I am fully confident in its current strenght and ability to prevent breaches of any kind, and yes that is while we continuously keep improving it such as with the newer cyber security branch as I am not so foolish as tinking that we can simply rest on our laurels.[/i]

With Thormod having said what he wanted and the other ministers reading through the papers they had been given and discussing it among themselves it was Amil Abdallah, the minister of Olia, that finaly spoke up to make sure they all remembered why they were there to begin with.
[i]While we have all now been well informed by the good General about how the information that our nation had a nuclear weapons program might have ended up in Tirakan hands we still need to reach an agreement on how to respond to their question about cooperation on said matter, do agree or do we disagree?[/i]

The ministers of the council would continue discussions for the rest of the night and into the next day with arguments for and ageinst it flying back and forth between them, but in the end a consensus was reached; they would cooperate with Tirakan to develop a functioning nuclear weapon as they all felt in some way or the other that a more powerfull deterrence would be needed for the future to hopefully keep the nation safe.
The minister of war would personaly send a reply on the councils behalf.

[b]{Encrypted Transmission to Tirakan - Naerim}[/b]
[b]{message: start}[/b]
We are willing to cooperate.

Grand General Thormod Thormodson III.
[b]{message: end}[/b]
